sentences.text: Central Bank of India are forged, fake and false.

On 13.10.2012 the petitioner availed over-draft facility of Rs.1,93,36,000/- (one crore, ninety three lakhs and thirty six thousand) from the Bank depositing the original title deeds and NOC dated 10.10.1012 of IDCO, Jagatpur, Cuttack Division issued in favour of M/s. Drink Well, of which the petitioner was the Proprietor and later on, it was found on a query from the IDCO that the NOC was forged and it was not issued by it.

It is further mentioned in the F.I.R. that the total outstanding dues against the petitioner in both the loan accounts was Rs.5,13,49,746/- (rupees five crores, thirteen lakhs, forty nine thousand and seven hundred forty six) as on March 2017.

On the written report of R.B.L. Srivasthava, A.G.M./Branch Manager, Central Bank of India, Janpath Branch, Bhubaneswar, E.O.W. Bhubaneswar P.S. Case No.
5 of 2018 under sections 420/ 467/468/120-B of the Indian Penal Code was registered against the petitioner and others and charge sheet has also been submitted under such offences.

sentences.text: // 3 // Learned counsel for the State on instruction submitted that as on 27.01.2023, the outstanding dues against the petitioner is Rs.12,59,00,000/- (rupees twelve crores, fifty nine lakhs).

Learned counsel further submitted that though the petitioner was offered OTS on 16.06.2020 for Rs.3,25,00,000/-(rupees three crores and twenty five lakhs) and he agreed to pay such amount, but such condition was not fulfilled by the petitioner.
During pendency of the bail application, the petitioner was granted interim bail as per order dated 15.05.2018 inter alia, with a condition to settle the loan amounts to show his bonafides and the same was extended from time to time and on 07.05.2021 in I.A. No. 428 of 2021, the interim bail order was extended till 07.05.2021.

Against the said order dated 20.05.2021, the petitioner approached the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in S.L.P.(Criminal) No. 3896 of 2021 and the interim order was extended till disposal of the regular bail application filed by the petitioner before this Court and accordingly, the S.L.P.(Crl.) was disposed of as per order dated 18.11.2022.
It appears from the order sheet of this BLAPL that the case has already suffered thirty four adjournments.

On 31.01.2023 the matter was listed and the learned counsel for the State filed written instruction from the Deputy Superintendent, E.O.W., Bhubaneswar, who is the I.O. of the case from which it is indicated that the Bank had intimated vide letter dated 25.01.2023 that the O.T.S. proposal for Rs.3,25,00,000/- (rupees three crores and twenty five lakhs) was accepted on 16.06.2020 and // 4 // acknowledged by the borrower
, however, the Bank has not received any amount even after their regular follow up and as such the O.T.S. has lapsed.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted on 31.01.2023 that another O.T.S. proposal was floated and in pursuance of which some of the mortgaged properties have been sold and the loan amount in question has already been secured and to that effect, he intended to file an affidavit giving copy thereof to the learned counsel for the State for verification.
Accordingly, the matter was adjourned.
Today, when the matter was called, learned counsel for the petitioner sought for an adjournment.
No affidavit in terms of the order dated 31.01.2023 has been filed.
Economic offences constitute a class apart and need to be visited with a different approach in the matter of bail.

2 public funds need to be viewed seriously and considered as grave offences affecting the economy of the country as a whole and thereby posing a serious threat to the financial health of the country.

sentences.text: (Ref: (2013) 7 Supreme Court Cases 439, Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy -Vrs.- C.B.I.)
In view of the nature and gravity of accusation, since the petitioner is involved in an economic offence, I am not inclined to release the petitioner on bail.
The prayer for bail stands rejected.
The BLAPL stands dismissed.

The petitioner shall surrender before the learned Court below within a week failing with the Investigating // 5 // Officer is directed to arrest him forthwith and produce before the concerned Court.
A free copy of the order be handed over to the learned counsel for the State for compliance.
( S.K. Sahoo) Judge PKSahoo Ranjan Kumar Padhi vs State Of Odisha ....
